label: input x at original position >= 5
explanation: Fires when the input token is the letter x during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position 5 or later (t = 5..8). Every such step is active (precision 1.0). Magnitude grows with position: mean activation share is much higher at t = 7-8, where top examples are near the max with x as the last original token (to_go = 0). x at positions 0-4 never activates it, and neither do other tokens, the delimiter, or the copy phase (even when x is fed back as an output). The only misses are 36 tiny activations (<0.03 of max) on other tokens at t = 8.

issues: No substantive problems found. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.9985, F1 0.9993 and mass recall 0.99994. There are 0 false positives.

The 40 misses on the test split (36 on dev) are all at t=8 on tokens other than x (u, i, t, 3, v, h), with activations of 0.01-0.02 of max and 0.0% of the activation mass. They are scattered, with no shared token, history or position beyond t=8, so they are noise.
The factual claims check out on the dev profile. Activity is 0 at the delimiter step, 0 in the copy phase (even though x is fed back there), and 0 at t=0-4. Every active step is at t=5-8.

The magnitude claim checks out. Activation per firing grows with t: t=5 has 10879 firings carrying 0.161 of the mass, while t=8 has 2804 firings carrying 0.184. Low-quartile examples are x at t=5 (about 0.17-0.23 of max), mid examples are x at t=6 (about 0.5), and the top examples (0.98-1.0) are all x at t=8 with to_go=0.

Minor wording point: the firing rate given x at original positions 5-8 is about 0.033 of steps, which matches x's base frequency. So the feature does fire on essentially every such step, and 'precision 1.0' is accurate.
